dialect.detail: Likely compiled with GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL); uses SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL clauses, INDEXED file with ALTERNATE KEY, IS INITIAL PROGRAM, and FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE — all consistent with GnuCOBOL on a PC/Linux environment. File path uses Unix-style relative path '../SCHEDULE-MASTER.DAT'.
evidence: ALTERNATE KEY IS CRSE WITH DUPLICATES
EXIT PROGRAM followed by STOP RUN

purpose.domain_detail: University course schedule inquiry system (UAFS - University of Arkansas Fort Smith context implied by 'UAFS' header)
purpose.summary: This program searches a schedule master ISAM file by course (CRSE), semester, and year. It displays a screen prompting the user for search criteria, reads the matching record using the CRSE alternate key, and displays the found schedule record including CRN, subject, time/day, building, room, and instructor. The loop continues until the user exits.

notable_features: SCREEN SECTION with LINE/COL interactive display
INDEXED file with ALTERNATE KEY (CRSE) WITH DUPLICATES
READ with INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY
Unix-style relative file path in ASSIGN clause
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — pure screen I/O
verdict.notes: Program header says 'BLDG-INQ.CBL' but PROGRAM-ID is SCHED-INQ-BY-CRSE matching the filename — likely a copy/paste artifact from a related program. The program_type is set to 'online-cics' as the closest match for interactive screen I/O, though it uses native COBOL SCREEN SECTION rather than CICS. Author and date (Zack Moore, 4/20/2015) suggest a student project at UAFS.
